codex_finding.title: Expire optional proof calls inside the shared FIFO queue
codex_finding.substance: When prompt searches overlap, the 70ms race stops awaiting enrichment but neither removes the queued get_episodes call nor cancels a running proof; abandoned optional work can block subsequent search_memory_facts calls past the native 300ms hook deadline. Fresh evidence on the reviewed head: a second search taking 150ms let the first search's expired proof start at 154ms; its 410ms response delayed a third search's fact request until 565ms.
codex_finding.disposition: FIXED at exact head 27b8d713e05ef592ea867c400a1d949fd02bd7a1 and regression-protected by two new tests using the shared GraphitiMcp client (not an independent graphiti.call stub)

committed_regressions.test: expired optional episode proof is dropped at shared FIFO dequeue before later prompt search
committed_regressions.mechanism: real GraphitiMcp FIFO (callTail) with mocked transport; first prompt's 70ms proof expires while a ~155ms second fact search runs; third prompt queued
committed_regressions.invariants: expired proof never starts (zero get_episodes starts), third fact query starts promptly, maxActive=1, exactly-once calls, FIFO order

committed_regressions.test: running optional proof aborts actual Graphiti fetch and frees FIFO for a new prompt
committed_regressions.mechanism: real fetchImpl observes the actual AbortSignal from GraphitiMcp.rpc(); a ~410ms get_episodes proof is aborted at its ~70ms deadline
committed_regressions.invariants: proofAbortCount=1 (exactly one abort, no retry), no index admission from the canceled proof, maxActive=1 (FIFO settles only after the abort), call order [search_memory_facts, get_episodes, search_memory_facts], subsequent prompt does not wait the full 410ms

independent_exercise.method: standalone scenarios against the REAL GraphitiMcp/Memory modules from the exact-head source (shared callTail FIFO; real rpc/fetchImpl paths; only the transport mocked where the named regression requires observing the signal)

queued_expiry.setup: Codex's exact overlap: fact #1 fast, fact #2 ~155ms, first prompt's 70ms proof queued behind them, third prompt created after the first resolves

results_observed.fact2_to_fact3_gap_ms_range: 156-174 across 3 runs (155ms search + dequeue; no phantom 410ms proof window; pre-fix signature was ~555ms gap)

queued_expiry.verdict: PASS: expired proof dropped at dequeue, zero get_episodes network calls, FIFO strictly serial, exactly-once

active_abort.setup: real fetchImpl with a 410ms get_episodes transport observing opts.signal; second prompt started once the proof fetch begins

results_observed.abort_after_fetch_start_ms_range: 62-94 across stable runs (design ~70ms; host-load timer slack tolerated, always far below the 410ms natural completion)

active_abort.verdict: PASS: real fetch aborted exactly once by the deadline signal; FIFO released only after the abort; no source authorization from the abandoned proof

initialize_signal.setup: fresh client whose first operation is a 70ms-deadline proof; initialize transport is slow (410ms) and observes the signal
initialize_signal.verdict: PASS: the real fetch signal reaches initialize() as well as tools/call; no FIFO release while a transport is active

two_arg_semantics.setup: stateful session (3 transport calls: initialize + 2 tools/call); every call carries the timeout AbortSignal; a scaled 200ms-timeout client with a 500ms transport is cut by the original transport timeout

results_observed.transport_timeout_cutoff_ms_range: 202-379 across runs (200ms scaled client; the 1200ms default path is the same code)

two_arg_semantics.verdict: PASS: non-optional two-argument callers keep the original transport-timeout semantics

independent_exercise.stability: 3 consecutive full runs PASS (bounded retry available; all structural assertions passed on first attempt in every run)
